## playbooks components actions

List playbook actions — the full cross-integration catalog, or one integration in detail

```text
secopsctl playbooks components actions [--integration <key>] [flags]
```

```text
Without --integration, list the WHOLE action palette in one call (the
`integrations/-/actions` wildcard catalog): every action across every
integration with its numeric id — the id `components usage` keys on. With
--integration, list that integration's actions in detail — `--json` carries
each action's full PARAMETER SCHEMA (name/type/mandatory/default/options), the
detail needed to author a step; the table shows counts, JSON/script-result
flags, and async status. Neither prints Python script bodies.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--grep` | string | - | case-insensitive filter over action name/description |
| `--integration` | string | - | integration key/identifier/display name (omit for the all-integration catalog) |

## playbooks delete

MUTATING (guarded): delete one or more playbooks permanently

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl playbooks delete (--name <playbook> | --identifier <uuid>[,uuid,...] | --from-file <path>) [flags]
```

```text
Delete playbook definitions by name or identifier UUID.

Single: --name resolves to the definition id via the live playbook list
(case-insensitive exact match).

Batch: --identifier accepts comma-separated UUIDs, or --from-file reads
one UUID per line (blank lines and #-comments skipped). A batch delete
uses a single API call and reports per-playbook success/failure.

Guarded: dry-run by default, --yes to apply. Deleting a playbook that
is attached to a case stops its execution — irreversible.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--from-file` | string | - | file with one playbook UUID per line |
| `--identifier` | string | - | playbook definition UUID(s), comma-separated |
| `--name` | string | - | playbook name (resolved to its id via the live playbook list) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## playbooks deploy

MUTATING (guarded): enable or disable a playbook

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.


| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## playbooks duplicate

MUTATING (guarded): duplicate a playbook under a new name

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl playbooks duplicate <name|identifier> --name <new-name> [flags]
```

```text
Create a copy of an existing playbook definition. The clone is disabled
by default (SOAR behavior). --name sets the display name of the copy.

Options:
  --folder  place the copy in a specific category (name or id)
  --env     override the environments for the copy (repeatable)

Uses the modern v1alpha DuplicateWorkflows API; falls back to legacy
DuplicateWorkflow, then export → rename → save on server 500.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview without mutating |
| `--env` | stringArray | - | override environments for the copy (repeatable) |
| `--folder` | string | - | target category/folder (name or id) |
| `--name` | string | - | display name for the copy (required) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | skip confirmation prompt |

## playbooks export

Read-only: export a playbook definition (save-compatible JSON, or a zip bundle)

```text
secopsctl playbooks export (--name <playbook> | --identifier <uuid>) [--out <file>] [--zip] [flags]
```

```text
Export one playbook. Default: the full definition as save-compatible JSON —
the same shape `pull playbooks` writes, so the export → edit → `push playbook`
loop round-trips and the file is the input `playbooks mold` /
`soar build-playbook` consume. --zip exports the platform bundle instead
(the format `playbooks import` takes — cross-tenant promotion / offline
backup). Writes to --out, or stdout for JSON.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--identifier` | string | - | playbook definition identifier (uuid) |
| `--name` | string | - | playbook name (resolved via the live playbook list) |
| `--out` | string | - | output file (default: JSON to stdout) |
| `--zip` | bool | false | export the platform zip bundle (for 'import') instead of JSON |

## playbooks lint

Static analysis: detect broken block refs, missing integrations, bad triggers

```text
secopsctl playbooks lint (--name <playbook> | --all) [flags]
```

```text
Analyze playbook definitions for common problems:
  - dangling step relations (stepsRelations references a deleted step — causes console 500 on edit)
  - broken block refs (step references a nested playbook that doesn't exist)
  - missing integration instances (step uses an unconfigured integration)
  - raw placeholders in JSON action params
  - whitespace-poisoned trigger condition values

--all runs across every playbook; --name targets one.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--all` | bool | false | lint all playbooks |
| `--name` | string | - | playbook name to lint |

## playbooks step insert

Offline: splice a NEW action step into a playbook definition after an anchor step

```text
secopsctl playbooks step insert --file <playbook.json> --mold <step.json> --after <step> --out <playbook.json> [flags]
```

```text
Add a brand-new action step to a local playbook definition: the mold (an
exported step — `playbooks mold extract`) supplies the wired action
body, the insert mints fresh graph identity (identifier, designer-style
instance name) and rewires the anchor's outgoing relation through the new
step. --after matches a step name or identifier; when the anchor is a
condition with several branches, pick one with --branch (the relation's
condition value, e.g. 1). No API call — review the result with
`playbooks validate` and save it through the guarded loop.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--after` | string | - | anchor step name/identifier the new step follows (required) |
| `--branch` | string | - | anchor branch to splice when it has several (the relation's condition value) |
| `--file` | string | - | playbook definition JSON to edit (required) |
| `--instance-name` | string | - | override the generated unique instance name |
| `--mold` | string | - | exported action-step mold JSON (required; see 'mold extract') |
| `--out` | string | - | output playbook JSON path (required) |

## playbooks step skip

MUTATING (guarded): skip one pending workflow step (the reject half of an approval)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl playbooks step skip --file <step-instance.json> [--comment <s>] [flags]
```

```text
Skip a pending playbook step so the workflow continues past it — the other
half of the approval decision (`step execute` continues it). Takes the same
step-instance JSON `playbooks step get` fetches; --comment records why.
Dry-run is the default and prints a sanitized summary, not the raw body.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--comment` | string | - | skip comment (why the step was rejected) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--file` | string | - | workflow step instance JSON file (required) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## playbooks summary

Read a playbook run summary for a case (surfaces faulted steps)

```text
secopsctl playbooks summary --case-id N --playbook <name> [flags]
```

```text
Fetch a playbook workflow-instance summary and surface its FAULTED steps —
each failed step's action, error message, and a Cloud Logging deep-link — so a
failed run is triaged in-tool without digging through the raw payload.

The easy form needs only the case id and a playbook NAME:
  secopsctl playbooks summary --case-id 123 --playbook "My Playbook"
`--playbook` is resolved to its definition id via `playbooks list`, and the
alert identifier is read from the case automatically (use `--alert` when a case
has more than one alert, or `--definition` to pass the id directly). Uses the
two-call pattern (list cards → get instance detail) for reliable results
across single- and multi-alert cases.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alert` | string | - | alert identifier (auto-resolved from the case when omitted) |
| `--case-id` | int | 0 | SOAR case id (required) |
| `--collapse-blocks` | bool | false | collapse nested block details |
| `--definition` | string | - | playbook definition id (overrides --playbook) |
| `--fetch-steps` | bool | true | include step details |
| `--playbook` | string | - | playbook name — resolved to its definition id via 'playbooks list' |
| `--show-errors` | bool | false | print full faulted-step error messages (default truncates) |
| `--steps` | bool | false | print the full per-step execution trace (every completed step, not just faulted ones) — for debugging a run that finished but did the wrong thing |

## playbooks test-cases

List SecOps playbook debug test cases

```text
secopsctl playbooks test-cases [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--environment` | stringArray | - | environment filter (repeatable) |
| `--page` | int | 0 | requested page |
| `--page-size` | int | 50 | page size |
| `--search` | string | - | optional test-case search term |

## playbooks trigger set

Set reviewable playbook trigger fields offline

```text
secopsctl playbooks trigger set --file <playbook.json> --out <playbook.json> [flags]
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--conditions` | string | - | JSON file to set trigger.conditions |
| `--cron` | string | - | set trigger.cronSchedule; pass an empty value to clear |
| `--enabled` | string | - | set top-level playbook isEnabled: true or false |
| `--execution-mode` | string | - | set trigger.executionMode |
| `--file` | string | - | exported playbook JSON file (required) |
| `--out` | string | - | output playbook JSON path (required) |
| `--reaction-conditions` | string | - | JSON file to set trigger.reactionConditions |
| `--trigger-enabled` | string | - | set trigger.isEnabled: true or false |
| `--type` | string | - | set trigger.type (JSON scalar, e.g. 1 or "Case") |

## playbooks trigger tags

Read-only: list the live trigger tag values playbook triggers can reference

```text
secopsctl playbooks trigger tags [--grep <s>] [flags]
```

```text
The tag vocabulary available to a Tag-Name trigger condition — check a
hand-typed condition references a tag that exists before `trigger set` +
a guarded save.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--grep` | string | - | server-side search term |

## playbooks validate

Validate an exported playbook JSON file before save

```text
secopsctl playbooks validate --file <playbook.json> [flags]
```

```text
Validate an exported SOAR playbook JSON file before a guarded save.
The command performs the same local save-shape checks as `soar push
playbook --dry-run` and reports trigger/step/action shape so the next
SecOps save or debug run is easier to review.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--file` | string | - | playbook JSON file to validate (required) |

## playbooks versions

Read-only: a playbook's saved version history (each save/deploy mints one)

```text
secopsctl playbooks versions (--name <playbook> | --identifier <uuid>) [flags]
```

```text
List a playbook's version log — every save (including `deploy` toggles and
`push playbook`) mints a new version. The identifier shown per entry is what
`playbooks restore` rolls back to.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--identifier` | string | - | playbook definition identifier (uuid) |
| `--name` | string | - | playbook name (resolved via the live playbook list) |
